rejected.title: Hypotheses and models
card: A scientific model is an explanation of how something works. It can be a diagram, an equation or a description, and it is used to make predictions.
A hypothesis is a testable prediction made from a model. It often takes the form: if the model is right, then this result should happen.
An investigation tests the hypothesis. If the results match the prediction, they support the model. They do not prove it, because a later test could still give a different result.
If the results do not match the prediction, the model may need to change. Scientists then adjust the model or replace it, and test the new version.
rejected.remember: A hypothesis is a prediction from a model. Results support the model or show where it needs to change.

a.q: What is the link between a model and a hypothesis?
opts: A hypothesis is a testable prediction made from a model
A hypothesis is a model that has been proven true
A hypothesis is a diagram that a model is drawn from
A hypothesis is a result that a model is built to explain
a.why: A model explains how something works, and a hypothesis is a prediction drawn from it so that it can be tested. A hypothesis is not a proven model, because it is only a prediction until it is tested.
a.clue: Which one is a prediction that an investigation could test?

b.q: A model says plants need light to make glucose. Priya predicts that a leaf kept in the dark will make no glucose. Her test finds that the leaf made a little glucose. What should she conclude?
opts: The model may need to change, as the result did not match
The model is proven wrong, so it must be thrown out
The model is supported, because plants need light overall
The hypothesis is not testable, because the result differed
b.why: The result did not match the prediction, so it shows where the model may need to be adjusted, for example if the leaf had stored light energy or the dark was not complete. One result does not prove the model wrong, and the hypothesis was testable because the test gave a clear result.
b.clue: Think about what a result that does not match the prediction tells scientists to do.

version.title: Hypotheses and models
card: A scientific model is a simplified way of showing how something works, such as a diagram, an equation or a physical model. Scientists use models to make predictions.
A hypothesis is a testable prediction made from a model. It often takes the form: if the model is right, then this result should happen when we change this.
If the results match the prediction, they support the model. They do not prove it right, because a later test could still give a result the model cannot explain.
Once the method has been checked, results that do not match show where the model needs to change, or that it should be replaced. A changed model is then tested with new hypotheses.
version.remember: A model is tested through its predictions: a match supports it, and a mismatch shows where it needs to change.

a.q: A model says sound needs particles to travel through. Students predict that a ringing bell in a jar will get quieter as the air is pumped out, and it does. What does this result do?
opts: It supports the model, but does not prove it
It proves the model is right in every case
It shows where the model needs to change
It turns the hypothesis into a scientific law
a.why: The result matched the prediction, so it supports the model. It does not prove the model, because a later test could still give a result the model cannot explain.
a.clue: Could a future test still give a different result?

b.q: An old model says heavier objects fall faster. Students predict a steel ball will land well before a wooden ball of the same size dropped beside it. In repeated, careful trials they land at almost the same time. What should they conclude?
opts: The model needs to change to fit the results
The model is supported, as the steel ball is heavier
The hypothesis was not testable, as it was wrong
The model is right, so the results can be ignored
b.why: The results did not match the prediction, and the trials were repeated and careful, so they show the model needs to change. A prediction that turns out wrong was still testable: the test is what showed it was wrong.
b.clue: Compare the prediction with what happened.

a.best: It supports the model, but does not prove it

b.best: The model needs to change to fit the results
